assessment: The incumbent supports the required CSV and works comparatively well with unchanged assignments: median handling is seven minutes there. Overall, 32/40 intended course sets and a 17-minute median miss the targets (D1-O1/O2). Assignment changes and renames suggest metadata problems, without establishing whether records are omitted or merely hard to recognize (D1-O3/O6/O7). Replacement delays greatly exceed execution time (D1-O5). A concrete limit is the unsampled split-course center: zero observed cross-center rows does not establish isolation or correct membership for that case (D1-O4).

openings.claim: Using current instructor assignments for historical weeks may select the wrong courses; renames may make correct courses appear absent during name-based checking.
openings.delta: Distinguishes selection defects from recognition failures before changing scheduling or speed.
openings.prediction: Assignment-change fixtures produce missing or extra course IDs if selection is faulty; rename-only fixtures retain correct IDs but trigger coordinator mismatch reports if recognition is faulty.
openings.probe: Use fabricated staging participants and paired unchanged, reassigned, and renamed courses for one week. Compare selected IDs with an independently specified roster, then have consenting coordinators check the documented CSV against supplied schedules. Record checking and importing time separately. Bound both probes within six engineer-days and existing hosting; keep attendance entry enabled and data private.
assumptions: Expected weekly membership can be specified independently of current assignments.
Internal IDs can be inspected privately without changing the CSV schema.

openings.claim: When a course splits during a requested week, does the export preserve agreed attendance membership exactly once while excluding other centers' rows?
openings.delta: Tests the sampling gap and distinguishes split-boundary omissions or duplication from isolation defects.
openings.prediction: A split-membership defect yields missing or duplicated expected records; an isolation defect introduces fabricated records owned by another center.
openings.probe: In the same staging session, define expected membership around a fabricated split, add another center with matching course labels, and export the spanning week while attendance entry remains active. Check ownership, exact membership, and import through the existing CSV schema.
assumptions: Coordinators can specify intended split-week membership.
Staging reproduces production selection and authorization paths; passing fixtures provide bounded evidence.
